system.boundary: Build a closed-loop lane-following system in Simulink that combines synthetic forward radar and monocular-vision detections, multi-object sensor fusion, detected lane geometry, coupled longitudinal/lateral model-predictive control, and a finite-mass vehicle model.
engineering_objects: Its acceleration and steering commands must drive the vehicle dynamics, whose updated state must return to the environment and sensors to close the loop.
physical_paths: Radar and vision vehicle detections must feed a connected fusion/tracking path that selects the relevant lead vehicle.
Vision-derived lane boundaries must feed a connected lane-center estimator.
The precise tracker, lane-fit, MPC, and vehicle equations are not prescribed, but the sensing, estimation, control, and vehicle paths must be causal and connected.
Its acceleration and steering commands must drive the vehicle dynamics, whose updated state must return to the environment and sensors to close the loop.
functional_paths: Build a closed-loop lane-following system in Simulink that combines synthetic forward radar and monocular-vision detections, multi-object sensor fusion, detected lane geometry, coupled longitudinal/lateral model-predictive control, and a finite-mass vehicle model.
Radar and vision vehicle detections must feed a connected fusion/tracking path that selects the relevant lead vehicle.
The controller must use the fused lead range and range rate for spacing control and use previewed lane curvature, lateral deviation, and lane-relative yaw for lateral path control.
information_paths: lane_following_input -> F90-XAUTO-09 plant/control path -> ego_acceleration, ego_velocity, driver_set_velocity, relative_distance, relative_velocity, lateral_deviation, relative_yaw_angle, steering_angle, collision
modes_and_events: Build a closed-loop lane-following system in Simulink that combines synthetic forward radar and monocular-vision detections, multi-object sensor fusion, detected lane geometry, coupled longitudinal/lateral model-predictive control, and a finite-mass vehicle model.
driver_set_velocity_mps is in 20--31 m/s, time_gap_s is in 1.2--2.4 s, and default_spacing_m is in 8--14 m.
Acceleration and steering must be the commands that actually drive the vehicle model, and all logs must come from the same causal simulation.
